title: Kernel hot-swap rounding and KV index mismatch investigation
creator: Marco Nguyen
description: Post-optimization regression: after adding hot-swap logic that switches between fp16-optimized and int8-quantized kernels at the prefill->decode boundary, we observe rare correctness failures where generated output diverges mid-sequence and the model emits repeated tokens or corrupted continuations. Root cause appears related to subtle rounding/numerical-drift differences at the kernel boundary that lead to an off-by-one in the KV write index (cache misindexing) under specific seq-len and batch-interleaving patterns. This ticket tracks investigation, repro, mitigation, and eventual fix.
reproduction_steps: 1) Checkout branch runtime/hot-swap-kernels with kernel-selection enabled
2) Run reproducer script reproducer/kv_mismatch_repro.py with seed 3782 and payloads with mixed sequence lengths (see repro harness link)
3) Observe divergence after N tokens (typically 10-2000 requests produce 1 failure) where KV read returns stale values and output repeats or contains abnormal tokens
4) Enabled additional trace logging (KV indices + cast-mode) to correlate kernel change moments with index mismatch
observed_symptoms: Intermittent generation corruption (token repeats / implausible tokens)
KV cache contains adjacent keys with unexpected offset (index i written as i+1)
Failure rate correlated with: mixed-precision kernel swap at prefill->decode boundary, batch interleaving, and long prefix lengths
No signs of memory corruption in ASAN builds; problem reproduces on CUDA + ROCm with FP16->INT8 switchover paths
hypothesis: Different kernels use slightly different rounding/accumulate order which produces numerically different softmax tails. The runtime uses a compacted KV write index derived from token positions; when a rounding difference changes a downstream branch (e.g. whether to compact a sub-buffer) the computed write index can be off by one under concurrent updates. The hot-swap path lacks a canonical boundary cast/normalization step, making it sensitive to platform-specific FP behavior.
impact: High - affects correctness for customers using model variants where kernel hot-swap occurs (hosted customers and Dedicated pools with mixed quantization profiles). Potential to surface as subtle hallucinations or repeated tokens in production. Estimated customer-visible error rate low but unacceptable for SLOs.
temporary_mitigations: 1) Roll back hot-swap by default: set runtime flag runtime.kernel_hot_swap=false in prod clusters (partial rollout in us-west1)
2) Force the canonical FP rounding mode at kernel boundary for affected kernels (platform-specific; added as a short-term patch)
3) Add canary checks that compare scalar position calculations at prefill->decode boundary and fail fast if mismatch detected
fix_options_and_tradeoffs: Option A - enforce canonical cast + normalization at every kernel boundary: simple and safe but adds ~5-12% CPU cost in the boundary path
Option B - unify kernel numerics by adopting a single reference kernel for boundary frames: minimal runtime cost but loses some perf gains from specialized kernels
Option C - change KV index computation to be robust to small numerical differences (e.g., integerize position before using): higher code complexity but preserves perf
Chosen approach: start with Option A as emergency fix (safest), then implement Option C as long-term robust fix to regain perf
tests_added: e2e: workflow in CI that runs repro harness on both CUDA and ROCm runners
comments: 2026-02-15 Marco Nguyen: Initial report from CI: two job failures in nightly stability suite flagged divergence after recent perf PR. Attached failing trace logs. Assigning to Aisha for investigation.

2026-02-16 Aisha Patel: Added instrumentation to log kv_write_index, kernel_id, and rounding_mode at boundary. Confirmed correlation between kernel swap and index offset in 12/120 reproductions. Created repro harness.

2026-02-17 Priya Shah (Runtime): ASAN run shows no heap overwrite; numerical differences visible when comparing qkv accumulation between kernels. Hypothesis: differing accumulation order in int8 path.

2026-02-18 Ben Ortiz (Infra): Deployed runtime.kernel_hot_swap=false flag to canary cluster us-west1-canary. No further regressions observed on canary in 48h. Rollback scheduled for production until fix merged.

2026-02-19 Aisha Patel: Implemented emergency canonical-cast patch and ran stress tests. Failure rate dropped to 0/10k iterations across CUDA/ROCm. Patch PR opened (1464), needs perf review before merge to prod.

2026-02-20 Marco Nguyen: Decision: merge emergency patch to stabilize prod, then follow-up with a robust KV-index integerization refactor (Option C) to avoid permanent perf tax. Add regression test to release pipeline. Marking security_review_required=false but tagging runtime-1.19 as target release.

2026-02-20 Design Review Note (Elena Cruz): UX for console alert: create automated incident summary when kernel hot-swap is toggled; will add dashboard card under Rollouts to show kernel-change impact per route. Filed DES-214 for console work.
notes: Follow-up: add a CI matrix job that runs reproducer with different torch/hip versions and with/without tensor cores to catch platform-specific numeric drift. Long-term goal is to allow kernel specialization without correctness tradeoffs.
